work.title: Symphony No. 9
work.movement: II. Im Tempo eines gemächlichen Ländlers

version.note: The recording sources identify the complete movement but do not establish the performing edition or any local alterations. The 1912 full score is used as a structural reference, not proof of the parts on the 1938 desks.

performers.note: Commons, the surviving concert-programme catalogue and the Library of Congress essay agree on orchestra and conductor.

date.note: 16 January is the documented public concert date. Pristine gives 15–16 January 1938 for its reissue; the inspected evidence does not establish whether any rehearsal material entered the issued matrices. The Commons embedded “1962” digitising tag is not accepted as a performance or transfer date.

place.note: The concert-programme catalogue names the hall and city; Commons uses Musikvereinsaal de Vienne.

label.note: Commons names only an unspecified audio CD. HMV made the original 78-rpm issue, but the CD label used for this upload has not been identified.

catalogue.note: The source CD catalogue number is unknown. Pristine documents the historical ten-disc HMV set as DB 8569–8578; that does not identify the carrier transferred for Commons.

matrixTakeSides.note: Pristine lists the original complete-set matrix series 2VH 7027–7046. The inspected DAHR composer listing did not establish a matrix/take match for this digital source; no exhaustive absence is claimed. Specific takes and a verified movement-to-matrix mapping remain unestablished, so the complete-set series is not presented as a side identification for this file.

credits.note: No engineer for the source CD or Commons transfer is identified. Gaisberg was the original recording producer and Charlie Gregory the recording engineer, not established digital-transfer credits. Andrew Rose’s named 2013 Pristine transfer is a different reissue and is not the source of this Commons upload.

date.note: No transfer date is established. The embedded digitising value 1962 is not corroborated as a transfer date and is not used as one; neither upload nor release dates substitute for it.

processing.value: Commons supplies an Ogg Vorbis file and an MP3 access derivative.
processing.note: Embedded metadata names Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20100325 (Everywhere). The original 1938 performance was cut on alternating wax-recording machines, but the intervening CD restoration, equalisation, edits and mastering are not identified for this file.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Ogg Vorbis from an unidentified audio CD

composition.value: The underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Mahler died in 1911. This is a term calculation for the composition, not worldwide clearance of an unidentified edition or transfer.

recording.value: Territorial: Commons applies PD-EU-audio to the sound recording.
recording.note: The inspected template expressly concerns expired performer and producer rights in the European Union. This package is admitted on that territorial recording-rights basis, not merely the composition’s age. United States status is not established; no worldwide public-domain clearance is asserted.

rights.creditLine: Gustav Mahler, Symphony No. 9, II. Im Tempo eines gemächlichen Ländlers; Vienna Philharmonic, Bruno Walter, conductor. Public concert, 16 January 1938, Großer Musikvereinssaal, Vienna. Unidentified audio CD via Wikimedia Commons; recording tagged PD-EU-audio (territorial, not established as US public domain).
